intro.data: A functor must also lift the do-nothing step to a do-nothing step. One lift here truly holds the whole batch unchanged (the lift of the plain identity); the other tampers with it — and then the Batch Cleaner jams on records it didn't expect. Use the faithful lift, then the Batch Cleaner.
intro.alchemy: A functor must lift the do-nothing step to a do-nothing step. One lift holds the whole crate unchanged; the other taints it — and then the Crate Smelter jams. Use the faithful lift, then the Crate Smelter.
intro.spellcraft: A functor must lift the do-nothing step to a do-nothing step. One lift holds the whole flock unchanged; the other warps it — and then the Flock Kindler jams. Use the faithful lift, then the Flock Kindler.
intro.abstract: A functor must preserve identity: F(id) = id. One candidate truly does nothing to F(A); the other tampers, so F(f) then jams. Use the faithful one, then F(f).

goal.data: Hold the batch unchanged, then clean it — using a faithful lift.
goal.alchemy: Hold the crate unchanged, then smelt it.
goal.spellcraft: Hold the flock unchanged, then kindle it.
goal.abstract: Apply the lifted identity, then F(f), reaching the goal.

afterSuccess.data: The faithful lift held the batch unchanged, so the Batch Cleaner saw exactly the records it expected. The tampering look-alike was the same type but altered the batch and jammed the next step. A functor must lift identity to identity: F(id_A) = id_F(A).
afterSuccess.alchemy: The faithful lift held the crate unchanged. The tainting look-alike jammed the next step. A functor must lift identity to identity: F(id_A) = id_F(A).
afterSuccess.spellcraft: The faithful lift held the flock unchanged. The warping look-alike jammed the next step. A functor must lift identity to identity: F(id_A) = id_F(A).
afterSuccess.abstract: The genuine functor lifts identity to identity; the look-alike does not. F(id_A) = id_F(A).

reveal.summary: A functor preserves identities and composition: F(id_A) = id_F(A) and F(g ∘ f) = F(g) ∘ F(f). These two laws are exactly what make a lift a functor.
reveal.moreFormal: A bare assignment of objects and morphisms is a functor only if it respects identities and composition. List, Optional, and Batch all do; a tampering 'lift' does not.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: map(id) === id and map(g ∘ f) === map(g) ∘ map(f) — the Functor laws.
